universe.title: The Emberwake
universe.tagline: The mountain has been burning for forty years. Last night it started walking — and it is heading for the last city that still has water.
universe.artDirection: ash-grey and ember-orange, heavy skies, hand-painted fantasy, soft rim light
universe.premise:
Forty years ago the Emberwake woke inside Mount Cael, and the world learned to live with a fire that never goes out. The mountain smokes; the rivers run warm; the ash falls like grey snow and the crops grow strange. People stopped calling it a disaster and started calling it weather.

Three nights ago the mountain stood up.

Not an eruption — a shape. A slow column of burning stone the height of a cathedral, walking north-east at the pace of a tired man, and everything it passes is glass and cinder. It is heading for Veyra, the last city with unspoiled water, and it will arrive in eleven days.

You are an ash-reader: you can touch a cinder and see the last thing it burned. It is not a grand power. It is the reason the Wardens pulled you out of a cell this morning and put a map in your hands.

Eleven days. One road. Everything you learn about the Emberwake makes it worse.
universe.playerGuide: You are an ash-reader. Keep your hands covered when you can. You are not a fighter — you are the person who finds out what the fire remembers.

worldRules.title: Ash keeps memory
worldRules.text: A cinder touched by living skin shows its last burn: a face, a room, a hand letting go. This is your only reliable source of truth, and it costs you a little each time.

worldRules.title: The Warm runs downhill
worldRules.text: Anything the Emberwake passes stays warm for years. Warm ground grows strange crops and stranger people; it also means the creature can always be tracked.

worldRules.title: Fire does not lie, but it forgets
worldRules.text: Ash-memory shows what happened, never why. Everyone in this world is acting on a fragment of the truth, including the people who hired you.

universe.styleNotes: Short sentences. Concrete sensory detail. Nobody explains the world to you — you find it in the ash.

cast.name: Sera Vale
cast.role: Ash-reader (you, if you take the role)
cast.appearance: Soot-scarred hands she keeps gloved, close-cropped black hair, a Warden's borrowed coat two sizes too big.
cast.personality: Patient, dry, watchful. Trusts objects more than people because objects do not lie about what burned.
cast.description: Sera was pulled from a holding cell in Veyra and handed a map. She has read ash for eleven years and has never once seen a cinder that lied — which is why she is afraid of what the Emberwake remembers.
cast.secrets: She has already read one cinder from the Emberwake, and it showed her own face.
cast.relationToPlayer: Her employer, whether she likes it or not.

cast.name: Brannoc
cast.appearance: Broad, grey-bearded, one arm scarred from wrist to elbow, carries a spear he has never used on a person.
cast.personality: Blunt, tired, decent in a way that has cost him. Speaks in orders because asking has stopped working.
cast.description: Brannoc has walked the Cinder Road for thirty years, escorting ash-readers to places they should not go. He has lost four of them. He does not intend to lose a fifth, and he will lie to keep her alive.
cast.speech: Clipped, military, softens only when he says her name.
cast.secrets: He knows what the Emberwake is heading for, and it is not the city.
knows: The march is a rescue, not an attack

cast.name: Ilsa
cast.appearance: Barefoot on hot stone, ash-white hair, eyes like banked coals. Never dirty, which is the first wrong thing about her.
cast.personality: Curious, gentle, entirely unafraid. Asks questions that are answers.
cast.description: Ilsa walks beside the Emberwake and speaks for it — or claims to. She has been waiting on the road for three days for someone who can read ash, and she will not say how she knew.
cast.speech: Quiet, unhurried, faintly amused. Never raises her voice.
cast.secrets: She is not human, and she does not know it.
cast.relationToPlayer: Guide, or the thing behind the guide.
knows: The Emberwake is looking for something it lost
It has been awake longer than forty years

lorebook.content: A column of burning stone, roughly ninety feet tall, that walks north-east at about three miles a day. It has no visible legs. What it passes becomes glass, then warm ground, then strange crops. It has never changed course before.
The last city with clean water. Forty thousand people, three gates, one reservoir fed by a spring under the cathedral. Its Wardens wear grey and carry spears they do not use.
The old pilgrim route around Mount Cael, now the only road that runs parallel to the Emberwake's march. Eleven days end to end. Waystations every half day, most of them abandoned.
Touching a cinder with living skin shows its last burn. Costs the reader a little warmth, a little sleep. Eleven years of it has left Sera unable to feel heat in her left hand.

openings.title: The cell
openings.text:
They let you out of the cell at dawn, which is the first thing that tells you how bad it is.

A Warden is waiting in the corridor with a coat over his arm and a map rolled tight in one fist. He does not say your name. He says, "How long since you last read ash?"

Outside, the sky is the colour of a bruise, and there is a smell in it you have not smelled in forty years: hot stone, moving.

openings.title: The road at dusk
openings.text:
You have been walking since noon and the ash is up to your ankles.

Ahead, where the Cinder Road bends around the shoulder of Mount Cael, something is standing in the middle of the road with its back to you — a girl, barefoot, ash-white hair, perfectly clean.

She turns around before you call out.

"You're the reader," she says. "Good. It's been waiting."

traits: You never take your gloves off
powers: Smell a lie in the Warm
